hardware_interface: 3D printed passive parallel-jaw handheld gripper plus robot-mounted compatible gripper and GoPro
pose_tracking: GoPro visual-inertial ORB-SLAM3 plus fiducial marker gripper width
modalities: fisheye RGB, GoPro IMU, 6DoF end-effector pose, gripper width, bimanual relative pose
policy_or_data_stack: SLAM pipeline to Zarr replay buffer; Diffusion Policy; relative trajectory action; latency matching
advantages: portable low cost in-the-wild data collection; robot-agnostic policy interface; supports dynamic bimanual precise long-horizon tasks
limitations: visual SLAM fragile in weak texture and occlusion; GoPro/SLAM setup complexity; passive gripper ergonomics and limited dexterity
china_business_relevance: core reference architecture for domestic data collection devices and ToB service SOP
notes: Original paper reports 780g device, 80mm stroke, 73 USD gripper BoM plus 298 USD camera accessories.

hardware_interface: standard handheld device plus adjustable robot-mounted device and fingertip extensions for multiple grippers
pose_tracking: Intel RealSense T265 tracking camera instead of open-source SLAM
modalities: GoPro fisheye RGB, T265 6DoF pose, gripper width markers
policy_or_data_stack: ROS nodes for synchronized collection and conversion to ACT or Diffusion Policy formats
advantages: faster deployment; less SLAM debugging; decouples from WSG-50 and specific robot hardware
limitations: T265 availability and long-term supply risk; tracking robustness depends on commercial module; paper short version has limited quantitative detail
china_business_relevance: good domestic product inspiration for a practical lab/industrial starter kit
notes: Website claims over 10k trajectories across 22 everyday tasks.

hardware_interface: UMI-like gripper with lightweight low-cost LiDAR integrated into wrist-mounted interface
pose_tracking: LiDAR-centric SLAM with spatiotemporal calibration to visual observations
modalities: RGB, LiDAR point cloud, 3D pose, synchronized multimodal data
policy_or_data_stack: end-to-end data acquisition alignment training deployment; still supports 2D visuomotor policy formulation
advantages: more hardware and calibration complexity than original UMI; single-author 2026 preprint needs independent replication
limitations: strong route for weak-texture industrial scenes such as white walls, curtains, shelves, doors
source_ids: Project site states cost below 5000 RMB and no external infrastructure.

hardware_interface: compact robot-compatible gripper integrating ViTac tactile sensors, force-torque sensor and pose tracker
policy_or_data_stack: multimodal sequence segmentation and event boundary detection
advantages: targets contact-rich long-horizon tasks where vision alone misses event transitions
limitations: higher BOM and assembly complexity; task coverage still narrow in public report
china_business_relevance: good premium module for cable assembly, insertion, wiping, polishing and other contact-rich data services
notes: Reports more than 90 percent segmentation accuracy on cable mounting.

hardware_interface: handheld gripper with compact six-axis force-torque sensors on each finger
modalities: RGB, depth, pose, finger-level wrench, grasp force
policy_or_data_stack: adaptive compliance policy predicts position targets, grasp force and stiffness
advantages: directly addresses force modulation and safe contact
limitations: sensor cost, durability, calibration drift and controller integration are nontrivial
china_business_relevance: important direction for domestic force/tactile hardware and ToB high-value datasets
notes: Submitted to ICRA 2026 according to arXiv page.

hardware_interface: handheld UMI-like gripper plus third-person camera view
pose_tracking: UMI-like tracking with added external visual context
modalities: egocentric wrist view plus third-person view
advantages: helps broad scene understanding while preserving handheld interface benefits
limitations: third-person camera reintroduces setup and environment dependency
china_business_relevance: useful for warehouses, retail shelves and large workspaces where wrist view is insufficient
notes: Abstract reports about 47 percent improvement across three broad-scene subtasks.

hardware_interface: 3D printed gripper powered by Dynamixel XL430-W250-T and U2D2 ecosystem
modalities: actuated gripper state and robot-mounted manipulation interface
policy_or_data_stack: Dynamixel API plus mechanical design files
advantages: turns UMI-like geometry into a controllable robot gripper; cheap and modular
limitations: not a full data collection pipeline; needs robot integration and safety validation
china_business_relevance: good reference for domestic small-batch actuated deployment gripper
notes: MIT licensed with third-party UMI components under their original terms.

hardware_interface: 25 USD reacher-grabber stick plus 3D printed parts and iPhone
pose_tracking: phone pose and visual data for Hello Robot Stretch adaptation
modalities: iPhone video and tool interaction data
policy_or_data_stack: open-source home robot stack and models
advantages: low-cost household in-the-wild collection; strong home-service positioning
limitations: embodiment tied to Stretch and quasi-static home tasks; not a general UMI replacement
china_business_relevance: reference for low-cost service-scene data collection product design
notes: Useful contrast: lower hardware barrier but larger human-robot embodiment gap than UMI.

hardware_interface: 3D printed controller matching target robot kinematics with off-the-shelf motors
modalities: robot observations, joint commands, gripper commands
policy_or_data_stack: teleoperated demonstration collection for Franka, UR5 and xArm
advantages: high-quality robot-native data; intuitive for complex manipulation
limitations: requires target robot during data collection and per-robot controller builds
china_business_relevance: near-term practical ToB offering for clients who already own robot arms
notes: Good complement to UMI rather than replacement.

hardware_interface: low-cost bimanual mobile manipulation robot with whole-body teleoperation
modalities: multi-camera video, joints, grippers, mobile base
policy_or_data_stack: ACT and co-training with static/mobile datasets
advantages: high-quality data for mobile bimanual tasks
limitations: expensive and environment-tied compared with handheld UMI; collection depends on full robot
china_business_relevance: benchmark for high-end data factory and mobile manipulation service
notes: Useful for understanding ToB data service when clients need robot-native demonstrations.

policy_or_data_stack: Diffusion Policy with rigorous evaluation protocol
advantages: shows data scaling can be quantified and sold as an outcome metric
limitations: not a hardware system by itself
china_business_relevance: supports service KPI design: success rate vs number and diversity of demonstrations
notes: Reports over 40k demonstrations and 15k robot rollouts.
